research_scope: Source-free context-complete mathematical equivalence review of common prerequisites; original candidate identities and the source wording are retained.

aliases.reason: Finite presentation of a module invokes two finite free modules R^m and R^n. They are a pair of instances of the common finite-rank free R-module prerequisite; the exact-sequence relation between them remains source-specific.

The representable-functor source uses the Hom-collection Hom_C(X,Y), and the finitely presentable object source uses Hom_C(X,M_i). Both are precisely collections of arrows with fixed domain X and variable codomain; set-valuedness is a separate local-smallness constraint preserved in the source contexts.

A total order on a field's underlying set F is the same general set-theoretic linear order as an order on S; compatibility with field addition or positivity of products is a further ordered-field axiom, not a distinct order relation prerequisite.

The two field-theoretic sources define an embedded subfield closed under inherited field operations and nonzero inverses. E versus F and K versus F are bound ambient field renamings; no algebraic, normal or finite extension hypothesis is implied by being a subfield.
